tagline: He never told me where he learned it
title: On the crate
journal:
The crate came from behind the chip shop next door. He used to drag it over himself, set it down square in front of the machine and wait while I climbed up. I couldn't have been any older than 4 or 5 at the time, and he had a rule that I had to hold the joystick even when it was obvious he should be doing it.

The trick was on the third screen. You stood on the ladder, not at the top, about two rungs down, and jumped left just as the thing came round. He said it into my ear like it was illegal. I went through about four of his ten pence pieces getting it wrong, and he never once took over.

I asked him last Christmas how he found it out. He said he couldn't remember, then said probably someone older showed him. Then he went and put the kettle on, which is what he does when he's finished talking about something.
prompt: Over the shoulder of a younger child standing on an upturned crate, the arcade screen lights the face of an older sibling leaning in to whisper the secret move.
